body.statement:
Consider a directed summary causal graph \(H\) obtained from an acyclic full-time causal graph of a dynamic structural causal model with maximal lag bounded by \(L\), causal sufficiency, and consistency throughout time.  For the singleton query \(P(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))\), if \(\mathsf{Adj}_{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,X,Y,\gamma)\) holds, then the effect equals \(P(Y_0=y)\) when \(X\notin\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\); when \(X\in\operatorname{Anc}_{H^{\to}}(Y)\), the set \(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}(H,L,X)\) is a valid adjustment set and
\[
 P(Y_0=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{-\gamma}=x))
 =\sum_a P(Y_0=y\mid X_{-\gamma}=x,
 \mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}=a)
 P(\mathcal A_{\gamma}^{\mathrm{ADGGM}}=a).
\]

source.locator: Theorem 2, equation (2), and Lemmas 5.1--5.3 in Section 5.1 of arXiv:2310.14691v5
source.verbatim_statement: Theorem 2. (Identifiability in SCG) Consider an SCG G^s associated with a DSCM with true (unknown) probability distribution P. Under Assumptions 1 and 2, the total effect P(y_t | do(x_{t-gamma})), with gamma >= 0, is identifiable if X is not an ancestor of Y or X is an ancestor of Y and neither holds: (1) gamma != 0 and Cycles^>(X,G^s minus {Y}) is nonempty; (2) there exists a sigma-active backdoor path <V1=X,...,Vn=Y> whose internal vertices are descendants of X and either n>2, or n=2 and gamma!=1, or n=2, gamma=1 and Cycles(Y,G^s minus {X}) is nonempty. Equation (2) defines A_gamma as descendant variables at lags 1 through gamma_max together with non-descendant variables at lags 0 through gamma_max. Lemma 5.1 identifies the effect as P(y_t) when X is not an ancestor of Y. Lemma 5.2 identifies by A_gamma under the negations stated there. Lemma 5.3 identifies by A_gamma for gamma=1 under the stated unique X<->Y backdoor and cycle exclusions.
